source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What makes a burn client comfortable for hydrotherapy dressing change?
questions.rationale: Pain medication 30 to 60 minutes before the dressing change helps the client tolerate a painful procedure.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q4 (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: The client should receive pain medication approximately 30 to 60 minutes before a burn dressing change.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding signals a complication of crutch walking?
questions.rationale: Forearm weakness signals radial nerve injury from crutch pressure on the axillae.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q10 (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Forearm muscle weakness is a sign of radial nerve injury caused by crutch pressure on the axillae.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Paracetamol liquid 450 mg is ordered; the label reads 160 mg/5 mL. How many mL are given?
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q19 (PDF p. 157)
questions.quote: After performing a medication calculation, ensure that the amount calculated is a reasonable amount.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the MOST accurate way to assess a weight loss program?
questions.rationale: Weighing the client at the same time, in the same clothes, on the same scale is most accurate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q38 (PDF p. 177)
questions.quote: The most accurate measurement of weight loss is weighing of the client.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which pain description suggests a fracture after a fall?
questions.rationale: Fracture pain is sharp, continuous, and increasing. Bone pain is a dull, deep ache; muscle injury is cramping.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q39 (PDF p. 178)
questions.quote: Fracture pain is generally described as sharp, continuous, and increasing in frequency.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on TPN has a finger-stick glucose of 425 mg/dL. What should the nurse do?
options: Slow the rate on her own
questions.rationale: Hyperglycemia is a TPN complication; abnormalities are reported to the provider.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q41 (PDF p. 180)
questions.quote: Hyperglycemia is a complication of TPN, and the nurse should report abnormalities

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's BP is 146/72. What is the pulse pressure?
questions.rationale: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic: 146 − 72 = 74.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q48 (PDF p. 187)
questions.quote: The difference between the systolic and diastolic blood pressure is the pulse pressure.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding shows a nasointestinal tube is in the intestine?
questions.rationale: Gastric fluid is acidic; intestinal fluid is alkaline, so an alkaline aspirate confirms intestinal placement.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q63 (PDF p. 208)
questions.quote: The pH of the gastric fluid is acidic, and the pH o

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which factor helps decide if a client with respiratory disease can benefit from progressive relaxation?
questions.rationale: The choice of relaxation technique considers energy, ability to concentrate, and physical capacity.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q76 (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Active progressive relaxation training teaches the client how to effectively rest and reduce tension in the body.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which intervention helps URGE urinary incontinence?
questions.rationale: Urge incontinence is managed with bladder retraining, scheduled toileting, and pelvic muscle exercises.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q79 (PDF p. 224)
questions.quote: Urge incontinence is the involuntary passage of urine after a strong sense of the urgency to void.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 50-kg child is ordered morphine 8 mg SC q4h. The safe range is 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/dose. What should the nurse conclude?
questions.rationale: 110 lb ÷ 2.2 = 50 kg; 0.1–0.2 mg/kg = 5–10 mg. 8 mg is within range.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q113 (PDF p. 262)
questions.quote: Convert pounds to kilograms by dividing weight by 2.2.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is done immediately before reinserting a cleaned nondisposable inner cannula?
questions.rationale: After washing and rinsing, the cannula is tapped dry and dried with tracheostomy pipe cleaners, then reinserted.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q131 (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: the nurse taps it dry to remove large water droplets and then uses pipe cleaners

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does the nurse start a 24-hour urine collection?
options: Have the client void and discard it
questions.rationale: The first voiding is discarded because it was stored for an unknown time; all later urine is saved.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q138 (PDF p. 288)
questions.quote: The nurse asks the client to void at the beginning of the collection period and discards this urine sample

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An NG tube stops draining. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Placement is verified first, then irrigation if prescribed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q142 (PDF p. 292)
questions.quote: the nurse verifies placement first to ensure that the tube remains in the stomach.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on TPN via CVC needs an IV antibiotic. What should the nurse do?
options: Give it through the TPN line
Mix it in the TPN bag
questions.rationale: The TPN line is used only for TPN to prevent crystallization and interruption; other drugs go through a separate line.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q146 (PDF p. 296)
questions.quote: The TPN line is used only for the administration of the TPN solution

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which behavior suggests a post-op client is in pain?
questions.rationale: Behavioral pain indicators include gasping, lip biting, muscle tension, and pacing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q147 (PDF p. 297)
questions.quote: Behavioral indicators of pain include gasping, lip biting

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which action is safe before a bolus NG feeding?
questions.rationale: After initial x-ray confirmation, placement is verified (tube length, aspirate) and residual checked before each feeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q152 (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: After initial radiographic confirmation of NG tube placement, methods used to verify nasogastric tube placement include

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: While advancing an NG tube, the client gags. What should the nurse check?
options: Inspect the back of the throat
questions.rationale: Gagging may mean the tube coiled in the oropharynx; the nurse inspects the throat.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q153 (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: the NG tube may coil around itself in the oropharynx

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which dressing is used on a burn fasciotomy site?
questions.rationale: The fasciotomy is left open to relieve pressure and covered with wet sterile saline dressings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q166 (PDF p. 318)
questions.quote: The site is covered with wet sterile s

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What does the client do as a chest tube is removed?
options: Take a deep breath and hold it
questions.rationale: A held deep breath raises intrathoracic pressure, lessening air entry into the pleural space.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q169 (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: The client is instructed to take a deep breath and hold it for chest tube removal.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client develops spastic contractions during ROM exercises. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Movement is stopped at the point of spasm and gentle firm pressure applied until the muscle relaxes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q176 (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: An unexpected outcome is the development of spastic muscle contraction during ROM exercises.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In which position is a bolus NG feeding given?
questions.rationale: The HOB is raised 35 to 40 degrees to prevent aspiration since the tube bypasses the gag reflex.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q180 (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: The head of the bed is elevated 35 to 40 degrees (Semi-Fowler’s) to preven

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is ureteral colic pain described?
questions.rationale: Stone movement through the ureter causes sharp, excruciating, wavelike pain radiating to the genitalia and thigh.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q184 (PDF p. 337)
questions.quote: is sharp, excruciating, and wavelike, radiating to the genitalia and thigh.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which foot care instruction is correct for an older client?
questions.rationale: Inspect the feet daily, including soles and between toes. Avoid knee-highs and prolonged soaking.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q188 (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Inspect the feet daily, including the tops and soles of the feet

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on TPN reports nausea, polydipsia, and polyuria. Which data should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: These symptoms fit hyperglycemia from the high glucose load of TPN.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q201 (PDF p. 355)
questions.quote: Clients receiving TPN are at risk for hyperglycemia related to the increased glucose load

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding shows a client uses the incentive spirometer effectively?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry reduces atelectasis, opens airways, stimulates coughing, and mobilizes secretions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q207 (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: Incentive spirometry helps reduce atelectasis, open airways, stimulate coughing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a dressing on an arterial leg ulcer be secured?
options: Kling roll taped only to itself
questions.rationale: Tape is never placed on fragile ischemic skin; a roll bandage is taped only to itself.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q209 (PDF p. 364)
questions.quote: Tape is never used directly on the skin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding indicates a need to suction a ventilated client?
options: Mucus bubbling in the ET tube
questions.rationale: Indications include visible mucus bubbling, wet respirations, restlessness, crackles or rhonchi, and rising pulse and RR.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q219 (PDF p. 374)
questions.quote: Indications for suctioning include visible mucus bubbling in the ET tube

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Foley drains a very distended bladder rapidly. What may the nurse do per policy?
options: Let it all drain at once
Clamp the tubing for a short time
questions.rationale: Rapid emptying of a large volume can cause hypovolemia or bladder spasm; clamping briefly allows equilibration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q232 (PDF p. 387)
questions.quote: Rapid emptying of a large volume of urine may cause engorgement of pelvic blood vessels

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After bladder repair with a suprapubic catheter, how are complications prevented?
questions.rationale: Urine buildup strains sutures; the catheter must drain freely.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q235 (PDF p. 390)
questions.quote: A complication after surgical repair of the bladder is disruption of sutures caused by tension on them from urine buildup.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which belongs in care of a client with a Pleur-Evac?
options: Keep the unit above the chest
questions.rationale: Frequent position changes promote drainage; the system stays below waist level.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q241 (PDF p. 396)
questions.quote: Changing the client’s position frequently is necessary to promote drainage and ventilation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A chest tube disconnects and the drainage unit tips and breaks. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: An underwater seal is restored first by submerging the tube end in sterile water to prevent tension pneumothorax.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q242 (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: the nurse should first reestablish an underwater seal to prevent tension pneumothorax

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Halfway through a cleansing enema, the client reports cramping. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The flow is stopped for 30 seconds and restarted at a slower rate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q256 (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: the flow is stopped for 30 seconds and restarted at a slower rate.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is gastric residual checked before tube feeding?
questions.rationale: Residual shows whether the stomach empties; a large residual raises aspiration risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q262 (PDF p. 419)
questions.quote: All stomach contents are aspirated and measured before administering a tube feeding

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The nurse aspirates 40 mL of formula before a feeding. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Residual contents are returned to the stomach to prevent electrolyte loss, and the feeding proceeds per policy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q274 (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: the nurse reinstills the gastric contents into the stomach

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After ureterolithotomy with a ureteral catheter, what should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Drainage is checked on arrival and every 1–2 hours; the renal pelvis has a small capacity.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q273 (PDF p. 430)
questions.quote: Drainage from the ureteral catheter should be checked when the client returns from the recovery room and at least every 1 to 2 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 1000-mL D5W bag hung at 3 pm runs at 75 mL/hr. How much remains at 11 pm?
questions.rationale: 8 hours × 75 mL = 600 mL infused; 1000 − 600 = 400 mL remain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q278 (PDF p. 435)
questions.quote: In an 8-hour period, 600 mL would infuse if an IV is set to infuse at 75 mL/hour.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before teaching cane walking, what is the priority to check?
questions.rationale: Balance, strength, and confidence determine whether a cane is suitable.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q284 (PDF p. 442)
questions.quote: Assessing the client’s balance, strength, and confidence helps determine if the cane is a suitable assistive device

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: 1000 mL NS at 100 mL/hr with a drop factor of 10 gtt/mL. What is the rate in gtt/min?
questions.rationale: 100 mL/hr × 10 gtt/mL ÷ 60 min = 16.7, rounded to 17 gtt/min.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q285 (PDF p. 443)
questions.quote: It will take 10 hours for 1000 mL to infuse at 100 mL/hour
